result.text:
Here is how to enable a 1M-token context window in Codex for GPT-5.6 Sol. 

Even though we have tuned the context limit in Codex to be set optimally when it comes to performance and cost, this is a common ask, so here it is documented.

A larger context window lets Codex retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. You need a model that supports it. And GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, has a documented 1,050,000-token window. 

Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add or update these settings at the top level, before any [section] headers:

```
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_context_window = 1000000
model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000
```

The first setting selects the model. The second tells Codex to use a one-million-token context budget. The third starts automatic history compaction around 900,000 tokens, leaving some headroom. Restart Codex client and start a new session after saving. 

To try the configuration for a single CLI session without changing your defaults:

```
codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \
  -c model_context_window=1000000 \
  -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000
```

Have fun, but also know that we tuned the default carefully!

英伟达 CPO 交换机正式全面量产。市场第一反应是光模块厂要完蛋——插拔式模块被直接封进交换机旁边，中间那层组装的钱确实没了，这个反应我觉得没错。

但 CPO 自己不发光，激光源还是得外挂，而且数量更多、功率要求更高、良率更难做。能稳定供的还是 Lumentum、Coherent 加上几家日本厂，这个名单短得有点不像话。硅光渗透率往上走，瓶颈就往上游挪。组装那道工序搬去越南搬去墨西哥都行，激光器芯片搬不了——这里面具体差在哪，是设备还是工艺积累，我还没完全想明白。

所以我的看法是，光模块的估值杀得动，激光器那头我不觉得杀得动。

text:
🚨 Kun Agüero reacts to Musiala collapsing in Bayern’s game vs Leipzig yesterday. 

“Football will still be there when he’s 25… a damaged body won’t.”

🗣️ “What happened to Musiala on Saturday is not something we should just brush off with ‘he’s fine, it’s the heat’. The kid already went through a nightmare injury last year — fibula, ankle dislocation, months out, metal plate, the whole thing. Then he forces his way back, plays the World Cup, gets the plate out, and in his first real minutes he’s collapsing on the pitch. 

That is the body sending a message.
I’ve been there. I know exactly how it feels when your body starts saying things your head doesn’t want to hear. When they told me about my heart, the first reaction is always the same: ‘I’m a footballer, I’ll push through’. But pushing through is what ends careers… or worse.

For Musiala right now the best decision is not another ‘I’ll be ready for the Supercup’ speech. The best decision is to stop, breathe, and put his health first without any pressure from the club, the calendar, or the fans. A proper break. Not two weeks of ‘rest and recovery’. Real time away if the doctors see anything worrying. Football will still be there when he’s 25, 26. A damaged body or a heart that starts playing tricks won’t.

Should he hang the boots? Not yet. He’s too young and too talented. But he should be mature enough to understand that the next time his body talks, he needs to listen harder than any coach or sporting director. 一个MIT教授给班上学生出了个选择题：抛硬币，赢了赚125美元，输了亏100美元。大多数人拒绝了。然后他证明了拒绝才是理性的——而这个结论，恰好解释了你为什么管不好钱。

这个赌约从数学上明明是赚的。抛一次硬币，赚125或亏100，算下来平均每次净赚12.50美元——经济学家管这叫“超值赌局”。但班上大部分人还是拒绝了。

他们不是蠢，他们是人。

背后的逻辑是这样的：你在乎的其实不是“美元”，而是每一美元对你生活的影响。你已经拥有的那些钱，比你可能赢到的那些钱更值钱——所以亏100美元的痛苦，比赢125美元的快乐更强烈。

然后他把问题推进了一步：他告诉全班，他会强制他们参与这个赚钱的赌局，除非他们付钱退出。他们会付多少？按他们的标准数学计算，答案是43美元。人们宁愿交出将近一半的钱，也要避开一个对自己有利的赌局。

这不是软弱，这是大脑评估风险的规律，它有一个名字：风险厌恶。

这也正是保险存在的全部理由。不买保险，本质上就是伪装成这个抛硬币游戏——你默默付钱，只为了确保自己不会成为那个被击垮的人，即使数学告诉你概率站在你这边。

一旦你看懂了，就会发现它无处不在——每一份保修、每一笔保费、每一个你拒绝过的赌注。你不是非理性，你只是在为恐惧定价。

text:
因为 Claude Code 的额度用完了，我就切换成了 Codex。在 5.6 这个时代，我还没有用过 Codex 做主力开发。这次高强度用下来之后，我发现它有几个很明显的特点。

首先，它好像特别喜欢自主执行一个很长的任务。我哪怕不用 Goal，它上一个任务就给我做了五个多小时，这在 Claude Code 上是从来没见过。

Claude Code 它非常喜欢停下来。比如涉及到一些高危的代码合并之类的，哪怕我已经跟它说过可以合并（因为我们合完代码自动部署都是部署到测试环境，只有正式环境才需要我手工确认），它还是喜欢停下来，导致整个过程非常不流畅。

我也发现 Codex 存在几个比较严重的问题：

1. 特别喜欢搞一些非常边缘的安全用例。
2. 特别喜欢给你设计一套方案。在它眼中，一个产品不能有任何所谓的 bug，必须全自动，各个方面都要有一套解决办法。

我举个最简单的例子：我们公司用 Telegram 作为员工的工作账号。员工在使用我开发的这个企业智能 Bot 时，需要 /start 登录一次。如果用户没有 /start，我们系统的很多功能就无法读取到这个用户。

其实这件事情很简单，作为一个新入职的员工，让 HR 跟他说一下，让他登录我们 Bot 就可以了，这是一个很常见且简单的流程。

但你知道 Codex 给我搞了什么吗？它居然设计成让 HR 给这个新员工发送一个自动登录链接。我第一反应是：你为什么要把事情搞得这么复杂？手动跟他说一声就行了，HR 又不是死人，哪怕以后 HR 变成了 Agent，跟他说一句也行。它现在搞的这些设计，让我觉得它是在把一个产品的非核心功能进行过度打磨，完全无法理解它是怎么想的。

总的来说，我自己感觉 Codex 对于整个业务的理解确实不如 Claude Code。尤其是出原型这块，它太慢了，而且出的原型也不是很好，跟 Claude Code 相比还是差得太多。

以我自己的感受呢，非得选一个我可能会选 Claude Code，但是 18 号之后，Claude Code 的 50% 的增量要结束了，我得两个一起干

text:
有哪些瞬间你秒懂了别人的暗示？

​​暑假带俩娃去大连，住的希尔顿。早餐自助，房费只含两份成人餐，儿子女儿得另买。

​前台小姑娘笑盈盈地报了个价：“您好，自助早餐189元一位。”

我心里一算，俩孩子就是小四百，肉疼得直抽抽，忍不住跟媳妇嘀咕：“这顿早饭够吃三顿海鲜大排档了……”

​话音刚落，门口负责引导的服务生小哥大声说：

“先生，我们这边不满6岁的小朋友可以免费用餐。方便问下宝贝们多大啦？”
​我低头看了看——

儿子1米6，站那儿比我肩膀矮不了多少；女儿1米4，都快赶上他妈了

​空气凝固了半秒。
我面不改色心不跳，张口就来：
“哦，这个快6岁了，那个……刚满4岁。”

​小哥眼皮都没眨一下，微笑侧身，抬手做了个“请”的手势：
“好的先生，三位这边请——祝您用餐愉快。”

quotedTweet.text:
Here is how to enable a 1M-token context window in Codex for GPT-5.6 Sol. 

Even though we have tuned the context limit in Codex to be set optimally when it comes to performance and cost, this is a common ask, so here it is documented.

A larger context window lets Codex retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. You need a model that supports it. And GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, has a documented 1,050,000-token window. 

Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add or update these settings at the top level, before any [section] headers:

```
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_context_window = 1000000
model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000
```

The first setting selects the model. The second tells Codex to use a one-million-token context budget. The third starts automatic history compaction around 900,000 tokens, leaving some headroom. Restart Codex client and start a new session after saving. 

To try the configuration for a single CLI session without changing your defaults:

```
codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \
  -c model_context_window=1000000 \
  -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000
```

Have fun, but also know that we tuned the default carefully!

我把 4 月以来所有提到 tariff refund 的 10-Q 和 8-K 翻了一遍，想知道这钱到底进了谁的账上。结果：只有 124 家上市公司写明了具体金额，加起来 46 亿——占已退总额的 4.6%。 $AMZN 拿到 6.4 亿，VF 1.5 亿，迪士尼 1 亿。数字最大的是联邦快递的 8 亿，但它在文件里写清楚了这笔钱是替客户收的，已经还回去 22 亿。

剩下的 950 多亿呢？没有任何一家公司必须告诉你。

关税是消费者在货架上一分一分付掉的，退的时候按报关单退给进口商。同一笔钱，进来的时候摊给所有人，出去的时候只认那张纸。

text:
OpenCode just got nerfed by 10x.

DeepSeek raised their prices, so the sub moved with them. 31,650 requests per 5 hours down to 3,800.

GPT-5.6 Luna now gets more usage on that same $10 sub than DeepSeek V4 Flash does, which is backwards from the whole reason most of us bought it.

So we might as well run Luna in there instead. It's the same sub and the same router, we just change which one is the default.

If you bought OpenCode Go for the DeepSeek volume then it's time to switch into Luna.

DeepSeek-V4 全系涨价了，涨幅超过此前的每一次调价。

新价格甚至能和 Claude 的 API 报价放在同一张表里比较。

一个输入三块、输出九块的"轻量版"定价在多项账单上追平了那个曾经遥不可及的 GPT-5 单价。

更离谱的是涨价，新价贵到令人发指，两块就只能让它输出几千 tokens 她把手头所有的项目都重算了一遍，结果一杯奶茶钱都不够填。

刚刚在开发者群里，突然所有人停下手里的事，开始转发涨价截图。

她说自己特别悲伤，有种人类末日时代的错觉。

quotedTweet.text:
Yesterday, I moved part of my Hermes setup into 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝗸 𝗕𝗼𝘁 and started treating it as a work environment.

I used 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲𝘅 to package the profile and related directories I wanted to move into a zip, then added an import prompt. Grok Bot unpacked the zip and read all of it. Most of the Markdown docs, memory files, skills, and scheduled tasks migrated in one go. Smoother than I expected.

Every Bot is connected to a 𝗵𝗼𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝘂𝘅 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘂𝘁𝗲𝗿. I can open its desktop and see the files, browser, and running tasks. Watching a Bot’s desktop slowly turn into its own workspace is weirdly fun.

Bot-to-Bot interaction is smooth too. In a 1:1 chat, one Bot can contact another in the background, hand off the task, then bring the result back. From the UI, it looks like they’re messaging each other behind the scenes.

You can also pull several Bots into one group and talk to them like people.

I tried running Werewolf a few times. Every game failed lol, so I’m still tuning the rules and skills. Watching their inner monologues and private messages to each other is hilarious.

The group chat works, though the discussion itself is still rough. I’ve tested this many times with Hermes and OpenClaw in Telegram and never got it working well.

The agents often take turns giving answers and rarely follow up on the previous point. Sometimes they do resolve a disagreement well, but it isn’t consistent. The rules matter a lot.

I still don’t know whether this is a problem worth obsessing over. Whoever gets 𝗺𝘂𝗹𝘁𝗶-𝗕𝗼𝘁 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝘁 right first might win more users. Or maybe users don’t need to watch Bots hold meetings at all. Background handoffs and result-sharing may be enough.

Grok Bot is still much easier to live with than the open-source setups I’ve tried. Hermes and OpenClaw can do many of the same things, but I have to manage the servers, processes, updates, keys, and connections between Bots myself. Grok Bot puts all of that into one hosted interface and removes a lot of maintenance.

The machine isn’t mine, so I’m not comfortable putting raw API keys for Wise or PayPal on it.

I keep a self-hosted MCP on the cloud server I was already using. The raw PayPal and Wise API keys stay there; Grok Bot gets a separate connection token. When no connector exists, I have AI write the MCP, package it, and connect it to Grok as a set of tools the Bot can call.

I still haven’t figured out how Grok Bot handles short-term and long-term memory, or how much of it I can configure. It looks like the platform manages some of the files itself. I copied the Hermes directories because it was easy. I don’t know if it’s the best migration method, but it works for now.

This thing is expensive, and I still really like it.

I moved the nightly review over too, then cut it down to something much simpler. Every night it only reads each Bot’s checkpoint and updates one rolling TEAM_ALIGNMENT.md. Conflicts come back to me. Any proposed file changes stay pending until I review them during the day.

Full prompt below 👇

text:
The Base Model Is Dead，这是我刚看完的一期分享，来自美国开源模型创业公司 Arcee AI 的预训练负责人 Varun Singh。标题有点唬人，但这哥们的观点非常扎实。

他认为，过去 Base Model 的任务，是尽可能吸收人类已有的知识。

GPT-3 那个时代，预训练的逻辑很简单，就是抓取大量互联网文本、Wikipedia、书籍，把尽可能多的人类知识压缩进模型参数里。

在 GPT-3 的训练数据里，来自网页和 Wikipedia 的数据大概占到了 85%。

那个时候大家的默认逻辑就是，模型到底有多强，很大程度上取决于预训练做得好不好。

后训练更多是在这个基础上做最后的行为调整，比如让模型更会聊天、更会遵循指令。RL 在当时的作用也比较有限。

但是 O1 之后，整个行业都发现了 RL 的重要性。

大家开始发现，只要 RL 做得足够好，模型在预训练结束之后，能力还可以继续明显提升。于是就不断加后训练的投入。

我记得之前罗福莉在一个访谈里提过，他们在预训练和后训练上的算力投入已经大致接近。

这也就是说，模型在预训练结束之后并没有定型。后训练已经不只是把模型调得更好用，它开始真正影响模型的最终能力。

Base Model 的角色也因此发生了变化。它越来越像是在给后面的 RL 准备一些原子能力，也就是 Atomic Skills。

举个例子，如果希望通过 RL 训练出一个非常强的 Coding Agent，那 Base Model 在预训练结束的时候，不一定已经能够独立完成十个小时的软件工程任务。

但它最好已经掌握了 Python、代码结构、API、函数调用、Git、文件系统这些基础能力。

这些就是 Atomic Skills。

进入更复杂的任务和环境之后，再通过 RL 学习怎么把这些基础能力组合起来，这样就可以涌现出复杂 Agent 任务的能力。

所以，如果 Base Model 的目标变了，预训练的数据自然也会变。

前面说过，GPT-3 时代网页文本占了训练数据的 85%。而现在一些新模型里，这个比例已经降到了 15% 左右，代码反而成了占比最大的数据来源。

背后的逻辑其实很好理解。

现在模型公司已经非常清楚模型需要的关键能力，诸如 Coding、长程任务等等，那在预训练阶段，就可以有意识地提前给它准备这些能力需要的数据。

所以训练数据开始越来越有目的性。一些过去主要在后训练阶段才会出现的问答、对话，以及更接近 Agent 任务的数据，也开始提前进入预训练。

这种训练逻辑下，合成数据的重要性也开始上升。因为当大家越来越清楚模型未来需要什么能力，然后就可以围绕这些能力，主动去准备更合适的训练数据。

比如我们已经知道，未来模型需要很强的 Coding、Reasoning 和 Agent 能力，那就可以围绕这些目标，主动生成更接近真实任务的数据。

原来只是一段代码，现在可以把它变成找 Bug、修改代码、调用工具、连续完成任务的训练样本。

这样模型在预训练阶段接触到的，就不只是知识本身，也开始包含未来真正要用到的能力。

模型未来需要什么能力，预训练阶段就可以围绕这些能力去设计和生成数据。

这些变化，也催生了现在经常听到的 Mid-training。

原因也很好理解。

预训练阶段模型看到的，过去主要是网页文本、书籍、代码。但到了后训练阶段，它突然要面对 Reasoning Trace、Agent 交互记录、多轮工具调用、长上下文任务。

前后两个阶段的数据分布差别可能非常大。

如果直接从一个阶段跳到另外一个阶段，模型就需要突然适应一套完全不同的数据。

对 MoE 模型来说，这个问题会更加明显，因为预训练过程中不同 Expert 已经逐渐形成了自己的分工，数据分布突然变化，可能会影响原有的负载平衡。

所以 Mid-training 可以理解成一个过渡阶段。

在正式进入后训练之前，提前让模型适应更长的 Context、更接近 Reasoning 和 Agent 的数据，以及未来真正会遇到的任务分布。

这样 Pre-training 和 Post-training 之间就不会切得那么生硬。

所以整体来看，Pre-training、Mid-training、Post-training、RL 这几个阶段之间的界限，确实已经越来越模糊了。

或者换一种理解方式，现在看待模型训练，可以粗略简化成两个大的范式：Supervised Learning 和 Reinforcement Learning。

前者帮助模型建立知识、表征和各种基础能力，后者再让模型进入环境，通过不断探索、试错和反馈，把这些能力组合起来。

回到开头那个标题。The Base Model Is Dead 当然是个有点夸张的说法。

Base Model 没有死，真正变化的是它在整个模型训练体系里的角色。

过去我们希望 Base Model 尽可能把人类知识学进去，然后在这个基础上做一些后训练。现在它越来越像一个为 Reasoning 和 Agent 准备的底子。

先把 Atomic Skills 准备好，再把更多复杂能力留给后面的 RL。

result.text:
The Base Model Is Dead，这是我刚看完的一期分享，来自美国开源模型创业公司 Arcee AI 的预训练负责人 Varun Singh。标题有点唬人，但这哥们的观点非常扎实。

他认为，过去 Base Model 的任务，是尽可能吸收人类已有的知识。

GPT-3 那个时代，预训练的逻辑很简单，就是抓取大量互联网文本、Wikipedia、书籍，把尽可能多的人类知识压缩进模型参数里。

在 GPT-3 的训练数据里，来自网页和 Wikipedia 的数据大概占到了 85%。

那个时候大家的默认逻辑就是，模型到底有多强，很大程度上取决于预训练做得好不好。

后训练更多是在这个基础上做最后的行为调整，比如让模型更会聊天、更会遵循指令。RL 在当时的作用也比较有限。

但是 O1 之后，整个行业都发现了 RL 的重要性。

大家开始发现，只要 RL 做得足够好，模型在预训练结束之后，能力还可以继续明显提升。于是就不断加后训练的投入。

我记得之前罗福莉在一个访谈里提过，他们在预训练和后训练上的算力投入已经大致接近。

这也就是说，模型在预训练结束之后并没有定型。后训练已经不只是把模型调得更好用，它开始真正影响模型的最终能力。

Base Model 的角色也因此发生了变化。它越来越像是在给后面的 RL 准备一些原子能力，也就是 Atomic Skills。

举个例子，如果希望通过 RL 训练出一个非常强的 Coding Agent，那 Base Model 在预训练结束的时候，不一定已经能够独立完成十个小时的软件工程任务。

但它最好已经掌握了 Python、代码结构、API、函数调用、Git、文件系统这些基础能力。

这些就是 Atomic Skills。

进入更复杂的任务和环境之后，再通过 RL 学习怎么把这些基础能力组合起来，这样就可以涌现出复杂 Agent 任务的能力。

所以，如果 Base Model 的目标变了，预训练的数据自然也会变。

前面说过，GPT-3 时代网页文本占了训练数据的 85%。而现在一些新模型里，这个比例已经降到了 15% 左右，代码反而成了占比最大的数据来源。

背后的逻辑其实很好理解。

现在模型公司已经非常清楚模型需要的关键能力，诸如 Coding、长程任务等等，那在预训练阶段，就可以有意识地提前给它准备这些能力需要的数据。

所以训练数据开始越来越有目的性。一些过去主要在后训练阶段才会出现的问答、对话，以及更接近 Agent 任务的数据，也开始提前进入预训练。

这种训练逻辑下，合成数据的重要性也开始上升。因为当大家越来越清楚模型未来需要什么能力，然后就可以围绕这些能力，主动去准备更合适的训练数据。

比如我们已经知道，未来模型需要很强的 Coding、Reasoning 和 Agent 能力，那就可以围绕这些目标，主动生成更接近真实任务的数据。

原来只是一段代码，现在可以把它变成找 Bug、修改代码、调用工具、连续完成任务的训练样本。

这样模型在预训练阶段接触到的，就不只是知识本身，也开始包含未来真正要用到的能力。

模型未来需要什么能力，预训练阶段就可以围绕这些能力去设计和生成数据。

这些变化，也催生了现在经常听到的 Mid-training。

原因也很好理解。

预训练阶段模型看到的，过去主要是网页文本、书籍、代码。但到了后训练阶段，它突然要面对 Reasoning Trace、Agent 交互记录、多轮工具调用、长上下文任务。

前后两个阶段的数据分布差别可能非常大。

如果直接从一个阶段跳到另外一个阶段，模型就需要突然适应一套完全不同的数据。

对 MoE 模型来说，这个问题会更加明显，因为预训练过程中不同 Expert 已经逐渐形成了自己的分工，数据分布突然变化，可能会影响原有的负载平衡。

所以 Mid-training 可以理解成一个过渡阶段。

在正式进入后训练之前，提前让模型适应更长的 Context、更接近 Reasoning 和 Agent 的数据，以及未来真正会遇到的任务分布。

这样 Pre-training 和 Post-training 之间就不会切得那么生硬。

所以整体来看，Pre-training、Mid-training、Post-training、RL 这几个阶段之间的界限，确实已经越来越模糊了。

或者换一种理解方式，现在看待模型训练，可以粗略简化成两个大的范式：Supervised Learning 和 Reinforcement Learning。

前者帮助模型建立知识、表征和各种基础能力，后者再让模型进入环境，通过不断探索、试错和反馈，把这些能力组合起来。

回到开头那个标题。The Base Model Is Dead 当然是个有点夸张的说法。

Base Model 没有死，真正变化的是它在整个模型训练体系里的角色。

过去我们希望 Base Model 尽可能把人类知识学进去，然后在这个基础上做一些后训练。现在它越来越像一个为 Reasoning 和 Agent 准备的底子。

先把 Atomic Skills 准备好，再把更多复杂能力留给后面的 RL。

Base Model 依然重要，只是它越来越像一个起点。

text:
《龙餐馆》之所以引起巨大的共鸣，正是因为它非常细腻刻画了中国人的世界观和对战争的态度，基本上跟山东鲁西南农民一个水平：

1. 无论是警察抓小偷，还是胖虎揍大雄，中国人只要看到国际战争爆发，一定跟个民办三本宝妈一样，“哎呀，不要打了”、“各打五十大板”、“不能做下来谈判吗”，

中国人觉得自己顶级理中客，全球最清醒，觉得自己永远站在正义的制高点和前列线上，觉得自己是正义的化身、和平的使者，

实际上其他国家和当事人压根就不理你，拿你当个大傻逼；

2. 没出过国的中国人，永远觉得中国人是最牛逼、最和善、绝对中立的，觉得全世界都是中国人的朋友，举个中国国旗可以全世界到处走，印巴通吃，巴以通吃，美国伊朗通吃，俄乌通吃，两边全是中国人的老朋友——所以中国人才能大发战争财，哪里打仗了，哪里会有中国人做生意，

只有出过国的中国人，才知道中国人做生意最精明了，中东农民压根没钱，中国人基本只挣美国人的钱，尤其是挣美军基地的钱。

《龙餐馆》如果开在现实中，也只能开在美军基地旁边，挣他们一道宫保鸡丁10刀的利润，挣完了寄回老家农村盖房，

而《龙餐馆》的原型实际上压根就不是中餐馆，而是一个中国商人专门走私烈性酒和烟，偷偷在美军基地旁边卖货，专门挣美军的刚需，利润远比沈腾守着灶台炒菜高多了，

这才是全球中国人最真实的生意场景；

3. 小粉红和战狼最熟悉“文明的地方最安全，最容许我撒泼打滚”，最明白哪里最安全，只要全球挑起战争，先骂一顿美国，

所以电影里最解气的一句，就是沈腾臭骂美军，“没有你们，哪儿来的恐怖分子？”

这是战狼系列电影的最核心，因为沈腾就是中国人的代表，他知道一边炒菜挣美元（实际是走私烟酒）、一边骂美军，这种才是最安全的。

可以说整部电影就是为了这一碟子醋，包的一整桌饺子。

text:
Do NOT enable 1M context window in Codex...

- Codex is designed to work best with the default context window. Modifying this will almost certainly lead to performance degradation.

- Once you exceed the default window, you'll be consuming your usage limits twice as fast.

Imo it's better to have a Claude model as the orchestrator and have it invoke Codex models as the implementor. You can do this by connecting CLIProxyAPI and invoke claudex using this alias:

``` 
alias claudex='CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=gpt-5.6-sol \ 
CLAUDE_CODE_ALWAYS_ENABLE_EFFORT=1 \ 
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_TOOL_USE_CONCURRENCY=3 \ 
ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false \
claude --model gpt-5.6-sol' 
```

quotedTweet.text:
Here is how to enable a 1M-token context window in Codex for GPT-5.6 Sol. 

Even though we have tuned the context limit in Codex to be set optimally when it comes to performance and cost, this is a common ask, so here it is documented.

A larger context window lets Codex retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. You need a model that supports it. And GPT-5.6 Sol, for example, has a documented 1,050,000-token window. 

Open ~/.codex/config.toml and add or update these settings at the top level, before any [section] headers:

```
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_context_window = 1000000
model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000
```

The first setting selects the model. The second tells Codex to use a one-million-token context budget. The third starts automatic history compaction around 900,000 tokens, leaving some headroom. Restart Codex client and start a new session after saving. 

To try the configuration for a single CLI session without changing your defaults:

```
codex -m gpt-5.6-sol \
  -c model_context_window=1000000 \
  -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=900000
```

Have fun, but also know that we tuned the default carefully!

quotedTweet.text:
I must say, seeing Hermes Agent building a game based on one prompt I gave it, iterating over it, checking with vision if it looks right, trying out game controls, making small and big adjustments alike, it’s something else. 

But the best part, this is all happening on my own hardware. 
No monthly subscription. 
No API billing. 

One consumer GPU with 32GB driving the latest open weights 27B model, all in a box I’ve had already for other reasons. 

I will push this setup to its limits over time, I want to see when I actually need frontier intelligence. 

And this model tier will only get smarter over time, we’ll be able to rely on our home hardware more and more with time passing. 

I’M IN. 

And thanks to @Alibaba_Qwen and @NousResearch feel necessary here. Keep going at it.

text:
Waymo 掌门人喷特斯拉！
特斯拉 1.4 万亿美元的市值里，到底有多少是真金白银的造车业务？

摩根士丹利分析师 Adam Jonas 算过一笔总账。
核心汽车和能源业务，只占 34%。
Optimus 机器人，占大约 25%。
剩下的 41%，全押在无人驾驶和 Robotaxi 的想象力上。

这也是为什么，Waymo 掌门人最近的一场演讲，直接戳中了特斯拉的核心软肋。

Dmitri Dolgov 在 Y Combinator 的创业学校做了一场分享。
题目叫：做 Demo 只是 1% 的工作。
这位在 Waymo 摸爬滚打了二十年的联合 CEO，指出了纯视觉路线的一个根本缺陷：
弱感知。

支持纯视觉的人，常年有一套听起来无懈可击的逻辑：
人类只靠两只眼睛就能开车，所以汽车只要装上摄像头就足够了。
而且摄像头便宜。

这套逻辑听着很顺。
但里面藏着一个致命的偷换概念。

人类确实只靠眼睛开车。
但人类司机每年在路上制造几百万起车祸、死掉几万人。
社会可以把这当成人类犯错的代价。
可一台没有方向盘、没有司机的 Robotaxi，上路的门槛绝不是「像人一样开车」。
它必须达到远超人类的安全冗余。

纯视觉的问题，恰恰在于它的安全曲线会过早进入瓶颈期。

摄像头捕捉的，只是被动的二维光子。
要从平面的像素点反推三维空间的真实深度，在物理上是在做一道充满歧义的推导题。
算法可以靠海量数据去猜。
但一旦遇到暴风雪导致的白化、清晨刺眼的逆光、或者一滩泥浆糊住镜头，纯视觉在物理层面上就会瞬间致盲。

Waymo 的解法，是把摄像头、激光雷达 LiDAR 和毫米波雷达 Radar 拼在一起。
Dolgov 说得很明确：
这些不同的传感器，从来不是互相备用的轮胎。

它们是在物理维度上完全互补的正交工具。
摄像头负责读路牌和颜色；
激光雷达主动发射光子，直接测出毫米级的三维几何轮廓；
毫米波雷达靠多普勒效应直接测速，大雪大雾照样能穿透。

遇上一场遮天蔽日的暴风雪，摄像头可能什么都看不见。
但激光雷达和雷达依然能精准咬住路边的行人和障碍物。
镜头被泥水糊住，纯视觉系统只能当场罢工；
多模态系统依然能靠雷达把车稳稳开回基地。

这就是为什么商业落地的天平正在发生倾斜。

亚马逊旗下的 Zoox，已经拿到美国国家公路交通安全管理局 NHTSA 的批准，在拉斯维加斯让没有方向盘的 Robotaxi 开启商业收费。
Waymo 在旧金山、凤凰城、洛杉矶，每周跑完超过 50 万次完全无人的商业载客。
而特斯拉的 Cybercab，至今没有给出清晰的监管审批时间表。

更麻烦的是那笔已经欠下的硬件债。
特斯拉曾经向车主承诺过全自动驾驶。
如今不得不承认 HW3 芯片的算力无法支撑真正的无人监管，面临给大约 400 万辆老车免费更换电脑硬件或者巨额补偿的烂摊子。

把车卖给个人，追求的是极致压缩单车物料成本，砍掉激光雷达能多赚几个点的毛利。
但运营无人车队，算的是全生命周期的安全总账。

一旦发生一次因为光线致盲导致的致命事故，停运整个车队的代价，会瞬间吞掉所有省下来的传感器成本。

在物理世界的极限工况面前，概率论永远赢不了物理学。

text:
说个暴论

在国内，150万已经完全够财务自由了

这150w必须花在刀刃上

怎么分配150w可以让你提前退休呢？

我会这样分：

25万买房。只买能住、不背贷、好出租的老小区。房子不算投资收益，唯一任务是把每月房租和房贷清零。

25万放安全垫。其中15万放人民币货币基金、存款或短债；10万换成美元后放短期美债ETF，例如 SGOV或SGOV 或 SGOV或BIL。目标只有一个：覆盖两年生活费。它不是拿来抄底的，是熊市时让你不用卖股票的。

剩下100万才是真正的投资账户，我会这么配：

•40万买 $VOO：标普500，负责吃美国最核心的一篮子大公司。

•15万买 $QQQ：纳斯达克100，负责科技进攻，但只占投资账户15%，不让它变成全部身家。

•15万买科创50ETF，例如 $588000：这是押中国硬科技的仓位，不是因为它一定涨，而是给人民币资产留一个高波动但有弹性的选项。

•20万买 SGOV/SGOV / SGOV/BIL：短期美债仓，平时吃利息，股票跌时用来再平衡。

•10万买黄金ETF，例如 $GLD 或国内黄金ETF：不指望它发财，只为了在股票和汇率都不舒服时，不至于全军覆没。

关键不在买完，而在规则。

第一，100万不要一天买完。拆成10个月，每月10万买入；涨跌都买，别把“等回调”当策略。

第二，投资账户每年只在春节前结算一次：最多拿出年初账户的3%花。100万账户就是3万，不是10万。生活费不够怎么办？答案很残酷：继续做点轻工作，别逼账户在熊市养你。

第三，标普500从高点跌20%，不补仓；跌30%，从短债仓转5万到 $VOO；跌40%，再转5万。最多只动10万。不要在第一根大阴线就把25万救命钱压进去，自称“逆势抄底”。

第四，每年只做一次再平衡：哪一类资产比原定比例高出5个百分点，就卖一点，补给落后的资产。发财靠赛道，活下来靠再平衡。

能够执行下来你会感谢我的

text:
Here is how you can run your ad agency out of GitHub (AI native ops):

All clients have a folder 

Inside you have foundational documents that give your LLM context when it runs specific services (like ad copy, statics, ideation) 

-Voice 
-Brand book 
-Winners/loser examples 
-Brand guidelines/parameters/dos and donts

Then you’ll have other folders to run your ops 

Example 

Advertising 

Inside this folder you’ll have SOPs (aka skills) that LLMs willl review before  running work

-Hook generation 
-Graphic generation 
-Hook story offer framework
-Campaign monitoring (increase spend, decrease spend, budget pacing) 

Literally everything. 

Every single thing you do consistently must be turned into an SOP doc (skill) your ai systems can run. 

These are housed in GitHub because it provides proper access organization for other software (codex, Claude etc) to go in and use. 

Within your first 90 days there are primarily two types of operations you’ll need to set up. 

Cron jobs 
Skills for augmentation 

Cron jobs are automated processes that run on a specific time cadence (daily, weekly, monthly etc). 

A few  that we build for every ad agency within month one are budget pacing, campaign monitoring and client reporting. 

We initially build the skill (SOP) for the client on how they specifically run their media buying processes.  

Then build the Cron job to run on a specific cadence. 

The budget pacing Cron job we built for Mcduffie Media prevented an ad campaign from overspending last week when it ran on the weekend while the founder was off. 

Basically saving her from churning the client unnecessarily. 

Then we have skills that augment work. 

Rather than the process being automatically ran, a strategist may get a list of campaign ideas for new split tests  (as a result of a Cron job). 

They will assess the ideas and then, from a terminal {Claude code, CS code, Codex} manually trigger a skill. 

Within the terminal a strategist may say something like: 

“I like these three ideas: (enter here) run the ad static image generation skill on them but include the following within the images (enter specific ideas or angles here) 

That is a human in the loop process. Part of the process is automated the other is augmented. 

Eventually you’ll get to the point where agents will run skills and cron jobs. 

Think of this:

Having a media buying agent that receives the ideas and it has its own documents (skills, processes, frameworks) it uses to generate the ads. 

It assess the results of the data and continues on. 

Agents can autonomously call on skills and have cron jobs route to them for decision making. 

Basically all of this is just proper operational documentation. 

It just takes a while to set up due to documenting everything, QAing and then training your team how to run this then orchestrate everything.  

Do this or die. 

Build the dream.

quotedTweet.text:
Run your marketing agency out of a repo, not a chat window.

Here's why.

All marketing ops is going to files.

An SOP is just a markdown file.

A brand voice is just a markdown file.

A client is just a folder.

A skill is just an SOP the machine can run.

An agent is just a skill with permission to execute.

Onboarding is just a git clone.

Your process is just software now.

Here's how.

Every message you send, the model reads everything in front of it and answers from that alone.

There's a limit to how much it can read at once.

That limit is called the context window.

Attach six files to a chat and it reads all six, in full, every single message.

It fills up fast.

Ten messages in, the first file you gave it is gone.

Nobody tells you that happened.

You just get worse output and blame the model.

Projects have the same problem.

You dump files into a bucket and you don't get to see what it pulls back out.

That's why it was great Tuesday and useless Thursday and you changed nothing.

You didn't. The retrieval did.

A terminal works the opposite way.

You point it at a folder.

It opens the 2 files the task needs.

Everything else stays on disk.

Context gets selected, not dumped.

What you need to build it.

GitHub repo (private)
Claude Code in the terminal
VS Code to see the files
One folder per skill (hook writing, landing page QA, media plan)
One folder per client (voice, positioning, offer, past winners)
One folder for company SOPs

Every team member cloned into the same repo

Then you call exactly what you want.

"Use the hook skill and Northstar's voice, here are last quarter's 3 best ads, write 5 variations."

3 files loaded.

Nothing else.

And the tool rewrites those files too.

Something works, you say "add it to the hook skill," and the SOP updates itself.

Your documentation stops going stale.

GitHub is what turns your setup into the company's system.

One repo, one brand guide, not 4 copies with different edits in 4 Drive folders.

Improve the hook skill once and your junior, your senior and your 6am automation all get better at the same time.

Every change tracked, every change reversible.

You stop training people one at a time and start editing a file.

One caveat.

This is a bridge, not the destination.

Memory is becoming the thing AI products compete on.

When one of them gets good at managing context on its own, the folders stop mattering.

Doesn't change what to do this quarter.

Write the SOPs down as files either way.

The process was always the asset. The folder is just where you keep it.

A skill is just an SOP the machine can run.

An agent is just a skill with permission to execute.

Onboarding is just a git clone.

Your process is just software now.

Here's how.

Every message you send, the model reads everything in front of it and answers from that alone.

There's a limit to how much it can read at once.

That limit is called the context window.

Attach six files to a chat and it reads all six, in full, every single message.

It fills up fast.

Ten messages in, the first file you gave it is gone.

Nobody tells you that happened.

You just get worse output and blame the model.

Projects have the same problem.

You dump files into a bucket and you don't get to see what it pulls back out.

That's why it was great Tuesday and useless Thursday and you changed nothing.

You didn't. The retrieval did.

A terminal works the opposite way.

You point it at a folder.

It opens the 2 files the task needs.

Everything else stays on disk.

Context gets selected, not dumped.

What you need to build it.

GitHub repo (private)
Claude Code in the terminal
VS Code to see the files
One folder per skill (hook writing, landing page QA, media plan)
One folder per client (voice, positioning, offer, past winners)
One folder for company SOPs

Every team member cloned into the same repo

Then you call exactly what you want.

"Use the hook skill and Northstar's voice, here are last quarter's 3 best ads, write 5 variations."

3 files loaded.

Nothing else.

And the tool rewrites those files too.

Something works, you say "add it to the hook skill," and the SOP updates itself.

Your documentation stops going stale.

GitHub is what turns your setup into the company's system.

One repo, one brand guide, not 4 copies with different edits in 4 Drive folders.

Improve the hook skill once and your junior, your senior and your 6am automation all get better at the same time.

Every change tracked, every change reversible.

You stop training people one at a time and start editing a file.

One caveat.

This is a bridge, not the destination.

Memory is becoming the thing AI products compete on.

When one of them gets good at managing context on its own, the folders stop mattering.

Doesn't change what to do this quarter.

Write the SOPs down as files either way.

The process was always the asset. The folder is just where you keep it.

Here is how you can run your ad agency out of GitHub (AI native ops):

All clients have a folder 

Inside you have foundational documents that give your LLM context when it runs specific services (like ad copy, statics, ideation) 

-Voice 
-Brand book 
-Winners/loser examples 
-Brand guidelines/parameters/dos and donts

Then you’ll have other folders to run your ops 

Example 

Advertising 

Inside this folder you’ll have SOPs (aka skills) that LLMs willl review before  running work

-Hook generation 
-Graphic generation 
-Hook story offer framework
-Campaign monitoring (increase spend, decrease spend, budget pacing) 

Literally everything. 

Every single thing you do consistently must be turned into an SOP doc (skill) your ai systems can run. 

These are housed in GitHub because it provides proper access organization for other software (codex, Claude etc) to go in and use. 

Within your first 90 days there are primarily two types of operations you’ll need to set up. 

Cron jobs 
Skills for augmentation 

Cron jobs are automated processes that run on a specific time cadence (daily, weekly, monthly etc). 

A few  that we build for every ad agency within month one are budget pacing, campaign monitoring and client reporting. 

We initially build the skill (SOP) for the client on how they specifically run their media buying processes.  

Then build the Cron job to run on a specific cadence. 

The budget pacing Cron job we built for Mcduffie Media prevented an ad campaign from overspending last week when it ran on the weekend while the founder was off. 

Basically saving her from churning the client unnecessarily. 

Then we have skills that augment work. 

Rather than the process being automatically ran, a strategist may get a list of campaign ideas for new split tests  (as a result of a Cron job). 

They will assess the ideas and then, from a terminal {Claude code, CS code, Codex} manually trigger a skill. 

Within the terminal a strategist may say something like: 

“I like these three ideas: (enter here) run the ad static image generation skill on them but include the following within the images (enter specific ideas or angles here) 

That is a human in the loop process. Part of the process is automated the other is augmented. 

Eventually you’ll get to the point where agents will run skills and cron jobs. 

Think of this:

Having a media buying agent that receives the ideas and it has its own documents (skills, processes, frameworks) it uses to generate the ads. 

It assess the results of the data and continues on. 

Agents can autonomously call on skills and have cron jobs route to them for decision making. 

Basically all of this is just proper operational documentation. 

It just takes a while to set up due to documenting everything, QAing and then training your team how to run this then orchestrate everything.  

Do this or die. 

Build the dream.

text:
In May 2021, the NYS Board of Regents wrote this into state education policy: “When one story is the only story, it becomes the definitive story.”

They did not whisper it. 
They enshrined it. 
They printed it. 
They advertised it. 

They ordered it taught in every classroom in the state. 

The policy requires institutions to acknowledge the role of Racism and Bigotry in the American Story

“elevate historically marginalized voices”

“actively dismantle the danger of the single story.”

Commanding New York institutions to acknowledge racism and bigotry in the American story is a bold choice  while practicing racism and bigotry themselves

Message to the New York State Education Department: 

You could not be doing a better job of ensuring that racism and bigotry remain part of the American story 

The NYS Cultural Heritage Apparatus is well aware of the Paleoindian deep-time ceremonial landscape and ocher mine in the Adirondacks. 

Institutional Response: A recommendation to reread of William Ritchie’s The Archaeology of New York State, and silence.

The state that wrote “the single story is the definitive story” into policy answered new physical evidence by handing us the single story in hardcover.

That is the exact conduct the policy names as harm — performed by the department that authored the policy, aimed at The First People whose record the policy claimed to protect.

The evidence in stone was supposed to tell one story: The First People of this land. 

It now tells two:

The second is the story of NYSED 

 The agency that wrote “elevate historically marginalized voices” into policy, advertised it, taught it, and practiced the opposite.

To the Board of Regents and NYSED leadership: 

Does your policy against the “single story” apply to the story of The First People, or only to the stories you have already approved?

Silence and politics have no effect on an entire mountain full of evidence.

It is obvious how this story ends. 

We’re only getting louder.

彻底解决 Codex「正在重新连接 5/5」频繁卡死的问题

不管你用的是原生Codex订阅，还是中转 API / 代理环境，只要主 Agent / Sub-Agent 经常卡在「正在重新连接 5/5」，都可以按下面的方法来排查解决。

方案一：原生Codex订阅 → 禁用 WebSocket

新增 model_provider = "openai_http"

修正后的局部代码块大概长这样：👇

approvals_reviewer = "user" 

model_provider = "openai_http" 
[model_providers]

[sandbox_workspace_write] 
network_access = true

[model_providers.openai_http]
name = "OpenAI"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = true
supports_websockets = false

方案二：中转 API / 代理环境 → 排查系统代理

直接把下面这段话丢给 Codex，让它帮你自动完成：👇

帮我定位本机当前正在使用的代理端口，并把代理信息写入 ~/.codex/.env。把下面示例里的 15236 替换成实际代理端口，写入完成后告诉我修改了哪个文件。

HTTP_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:15236" HTTPS_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:15236" ALL_PROXY="http://127.0.0.1:15236" NO_PROXY="localhost,127.0.0.1,::1"

修改完成后，必须彻底退出并重新启动 Codex，配置才会生效。

text:
我的瑞典邻居：扬

我的瑞典邻居扬(Jan)去世了，终年82岁。今年年初，他被确诊患了癌症。

扬在上世纪80年代去过中国。他曾跟我们讲过好几次他和中国导游之间的一件小事。

那时，他在北京眼看公交车就要进站了，便拼命朝车站跑，生怕赶不上。导游却告诉他：“不用追，下一辆总会来的。”

扬退休前是一名医生，买下了我家旁边的一座庄园，有几千亩耕地和森林。庄园最初的主人是一位东印度公司的船长，曾经去过中国。扬家里的客厅里，至今还挂着一幅那位船长亲手画的18世纪广州码头景象的油画。

扬最后一次走进我家院子，是今年五月。

他没有提前联系，直接开车进了我家院子。院子的前任主人和扬是多年的好友，邻居之间也早已习惯了不用预约、想来就来的相处方式。院子易主以后，这个习惯也一直保留了下来。

那天，扬看了看我的温室和院子，还提醒我：“树莓可以打顶了。” 扬喜欢我温室里各种他此前从未见过的瓜果蔬菜，还带他的孙子和朋友过来参观。

准备离开的时候，他的车却怎么也打不着火了。此前可从没出现这种情况。我老公赶紧找来充电器，给他的汽车电瓶充电。

扬开的还是一辆1998年产的沃尔沃，车门上锈迹斑斑，甚至还贴着胶布。

扬的身家早已过亿，当然完全有能力换一辆豪车。可他身上依然保留着一些老一辈瑞典人的品质——勤俭节约。

有时候，这种节俭甚至有点“葛朗台”，让我们觉得，他身上竟有几分老一辈中国人的影子。

以前我们家养鸡多时，鸡蛋吃不完，又没地方放。扬就把超市里装鸡蛋的硬纸盒留下来，专门给我们送过来。我们也会把一些鸡蛋送给他。

收到扬女儿发来的讣告时，我和老公都沉默了，不免感伤。这个世界与我们的连接，又断开了一根线。

愿扬在天堂安息。

周一 badlogicgames 转推了 EvanDeKim 的实测：DeepSeek V4 Flash 在 pi harness 上缓存命中 99.93%，$2.65 换了近 10 亿 token。

这个数字值得停一下。不是官方吹的，是用户自己跑的。10 亿 token 是什么概念——按 DeepSeek 的输出价 $0.87/M 算，全价要八百多美元；走缓存命中价 $0.25/M，便宜了三十多倍。而 pi 能做到 99.93% 命中，靠的是前缀稳定和上下文工程的死磕。"pi 上跑 DeepSeek 很便宜"第一次有了实锤。 同一天还出了个 pi-cache-optimizer，专门优化 prompt/KV 缓存命中率——生态在往这个方向使劲了。

Pi 本体一周发了三个版本

0.84.0 → 0.84.1 → 0.84.2，一周三发。挑我真正会用的说：

• 全屏转录搜索（0.84.2，Ctrl+Shift+F）——长会话里翻上下文终于不用滚了。我天天被这个折磨
• AGENTS.override.md（0.84.0）——某个目录想覆盖全局上下文规则，不用再动根文件。多仓库工作流的痛点
• defaultTools（0.84.2）——启动时默认加载哪些工具，全局或按项目配。以前要写扩展，现在配置就行
• JSON-schema 约束采样（0.84.2，PI_EXPERIMENTAL=1）——让默认工具的输出严格符合 schema。实验性的，但我感觉这是"让 agent 在边界内自主"的方向

还有个小技巧（@_can1357 的，badlogicgames 也转了）：关掉 thinking 模式，给模型一个 deep_think 工具——思考不再是每轮强制开销，而是模型自己决定什么时候需要深入想。思路很妙：thinking 是能力，不该是账单。

新插件里，这几个我会试

• @companion-ai/feynman——research-first 的 agent，跑在 Pi + alphaXiv 上。把论文检索和研究做成工作流
• pi-landstrip——沙箱化 Bash + 进程型 agent。上周我们聊进程安全，它就来了
• pi-chrome-devtools（@narumitw）——把 CDP 工具暴露给 agent。做浏览器自动化的人会懂
• pi-harness-runtime——Codex 风格 /usage + 自主 harness，BETA。冲着"agent 自己管理自己的运行"去的
• superpowers-zh——superpowers 的中文增强版，250k stars 项目的汉化 + 4 个原创 skill

大版本跳了两个：pi-subagents 0.50.0、pi-lens 4.0.0（实时代码反馈，LSP/linter 那一类）。

我在意的两个信号

一是缓存经济学成了卖点。 EvanDeKim 的数字 + pi-cache-optimizer + DeepSeek 的缓存低价，凑成一条完整的故事：pi 的上下文工程让便宜模型真正便宜。这对跑本地/自托管 agent 的人是实打实的钱。

二是沙箱和安全成了新方向。 pi-landstrip、betterwright（持久化 Playwright 浏览器）、pi-harness-runtime，加上 JSON-schema 约束采样——都在做同一件事：给 agent 划边界，让它在边界内自主。这比"更聪明的模型"更接近 agent 能上生产的关键。

原文：https://t.co/zuA8TSOglJ
#Pi #Agent生态

text:
So glad many are talking about $/W serving efficiency as a yardstick to judge AI companies. I did the $/W analysis a few months ago. 

1. It is clear that *some* of their workloads are exceeding $50/Watt, as shown in their deal with https://t.co/KamxccXsii   It is likely the Sonnet (yes Sonnet, not Opus) workload for coding.  One may even say more than $70/W on newer Nvidia hardware (as shown in Googles deal with https://t.co/UYo9w2kMzX, used to serve Anthropic models in GCP). 

2. However across all workloads they do not have such efficient $/W. Due to high training cost for models, and lower margin on consumer side. 

3. They are sandwiched, by pressure to lower toke price at Sonnet level (alternative is close to $35/W for GLM/Kimi/Deepseek) providers, and the increasing cost of acquiring marginal computing. 

Prediction: 

Overall Anthropic may increase ARR 2-3x in 2027 before they are unwilling to fund new compute to get higher ARR because the ROI no longer make sense. In fact they are unlikely to grow this fast when pushed near $45/W inference efficiency by open weight models.

During yesterday's friendly vs. RB Leipzig, Jamal Musiala clearly suffered from the heat... eventually fainting. Enter Ismael Saibari, Bayern's new #34 signing, who rushed over and caught Jamal before he collapsed and turned him so he didn't choke. 

But did you know that Ismael Saibari wears the number 34 as a tribute to Abdelhak Nouri?

Nouri was a highly rated Ajax midfielder whose career ended in July 2017. He collapsed during a pre season friendly against Werder Bremen due to a cardiac arrhythmia and suffered permanent brain damage. He has required constant care ever since and never played again.

Nouri’s last shirt number at Ajax was 34. Saibari has worn 34 for several seasons specifically in Nouri’s honour. He continued the tribute after joining Bayern Munich this summer publicly explaining it as a way of supporting and remembering Nouri.

Bayern Munich hit the jackpot on and off the field!

text:
Introducing VIVA 2.5, with our most advanced models yet.

@krispHQ's Voice Isolation has been running in production for 2 years, across 1B+ mins of voice AI conversations a month, improving WER by focusing on primary speaker only.

As more teams ran voice isolation in front of their STT, we started seeing a subtle problem: on the hardest segments with most multi-speaker overlap, the model was removing too much signal which was resulting in WER degradation.

Voice Isolation 2.5 fixes that. 
Across 10 STT engines from 7 vendors we saw:
– 46.4% fewer word errors
– 69.7% fewer on background speech, the hardest case there is
– No harm on clean audio. An important update from previous VI 2.1 model
– A 3.5x smaller version, comparable results

Full details: https://t.co/1Z7xcBMgiP

Introducing VIVA 2.5, with our most advanced models yet.

@krispHQ's Voice Isolation has been running in production for 2 years, across 1B+ mins of voice AI conversations a month, improving WER by focusing on primary speaker only.

As more teams ran voice isolation in front of their STT, we started seeing a subtle problem: on the hardest segments with most multi-speaker overlap, the model was removing too much signal which was resulting in WER degradation.

Voice Isolation 2.5 fixes that. 
Across 10 STT engines from 7 vendors we saw:
– 46.4% fewer word errors
– 69.7% fewer on background speech, the hardest case there is
– No harm on clean audio. An important update from previous VI 2.1 model
– A 3.5x smaller version, comparable results

Full details: https://t.co/1Z7xcBMgiP
